# Sirach Chapter 11 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_011_page_001.jpg

---

**11:1** The wisdom of the humble will lift up his head, and seat him among great men.

**11:2** Do not praise a man for his appearance, nor despise anyone on account of how he looks.

**11:3** The bee is small among all that flies, yet what it produces is the finest of sweet things.

**11:4** Do not boast about the clothes you wear, or exalt yourself on your day of honor; for the works of the LORD are marvelous, and his works among people remain hidden.

**11:5** Many kings have been brought down to the ground, while someone never thought of has worn the crown.

**11:6** Many powerful men have been greatly disgraced, and those renowned have been handed over to the power of others.

**11:7** Before investigating, do not find fault; examine the matter first, and then reprove.

**11:8** Before you hear, do not answer, and in the middle of speaking do not interrupt.

**11:9** Do not quarrel over what does not concern you, and do not sit in judgment with sinners.

**11:10** My child, do not take on too many matters; if you multiply activities, you will not go unpunished. If you pursue, you will not overtake; and you will not escape by fleeing.

**11:11** There is one who labors and toils and hurries, yet falls further behind.

**11:12** There is one who is sluggish and needs help, who lacks strength and falls short — yet the eye of the LORD looks upon him for good, and raises him up from his low condition.

**11:13** He lifts his head, and many are astonished at him.

**11:14** Good and evil, life and death, poverty and wealth — all are from the LORD.

**11:15** The LORD's gift remains with the devout, and his favor leads to enduring success.

**11:16** There is one who grows rich through careful attention — and this is the portion of his reward.

**11:17** There is one who stays poor through excessive frugality — and this is his appointed lot.

**11:18** There is one who grows rich through miserliness — and this is what he will receive:

**11:19** When he says, "I have found rest, and now I will enjoy my goods" — he does not know when his time will come, and he will leave them to others and die.

**11:20** Stand firm in your commitment and attend to it, and grow old in your work.

**11:21** Do not be awed by the deeds of a sinner; trust in the LORD and keep at your task, for it is easy in the LORD's eyes to make a poor person suddenly rich.

**11:22** The LORD's blessing is the reward of the devout, and in a moment he makes his blessing flourish.

**11:23** Do not say, "What do I need, and what benefit will come to me hereafter?"

**11:24** Do not say, "I am self-sufficient — what harm could befall me now?"

**11:25** In the day of good things, evil is forgotten; and in the day of evil, good things are not remembered.

**11:26** For it is easy before the LORD to repay each person on the day of death according to their ways.

**11:27** An hour of affliction causes one to forget pleasure; at the end, a person's deeds are revealed.

**11:28** Do not call anyone blessed before his death — a man will be known by his end, and by his children.

**11:29** Do not bring just anyone into your home, for the crafty set many a snare.

**11:30** Like a caged decoy partridge, so is the heart of the proud — like a spy, he watches for your downfall.

**11:31** He turns good into evil, and attaches blame to whatever is praiseworthy.

**11:32** From a single spark a great fire is kindled, and a sinner lies in wait for blood.

**11:33** Guard yourself against a bad person, for he contrives evil, lest he give you a permanent stain.

**11:34** Bring a stranger into your home and he will throw you into turmoil, and estrange you from your own household.
